office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital, and transportation budgets, including school funding, taxes, housing, and criminal statutes.
race_blurb: First-term Republican Joshua Penner, a former Orting mayor, faces Democrat John Bielka, a civil engineer and public works director. Both run on fiscal accountability, and Bielka says he will not back tax increases until spending is prioritized.

candidates.summary: First-term state representative, former eight-year Orting mayor, and Marine Iraq War veteran, running on oversight of state agencies and lowering living costs.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026 income tax over $1 million) and ESHB 1296 (2025) [S4][S5]
Opposed SB 6309, which he says lets Sound Transit sidestep local zoning [S2]
Cites saving Buckley's Rainier School and funding the White River and Fairfax bridge repairs [S1]

taxes.basis: Voted against the 2026 income tax and pledges to lower living costs; no broader tax-cut platform stated.

spending.basis: Runs on 'data-driven oversight' and demanding accountability and return on investment from state agencies.

local-control.basis: Opposed letting Sound Transit sidestep local zoning, and offered amendments to shield local governments from Attorney General demands.

experience.basis: First-term legislator with eight years as mayor and six on the city council, against a first-time candidate.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296's amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list; no separate campaign statement.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate, civil engineer and public works director with 30+ years in infrastructure and budgets, running on practical results, housing supply, and budget discipline.
highlights: Will not support increased taxes until the Legislature prioritizes its spending [S3]
Supports ADUs, duplexes, townhomes, and predictable permitting to add housing [S3]
Supports the Second Amendment and responsible gun ownership [S2]

taxes.basis: Says he will not support tax increases until the Legislature prioritizes spending, quoting 'a spending problem, not a revenue problem.'

spending.basis: Calls for measuring results and ending programs that fail to deliver, while prioritizing maintenance of existing infrastructure.

housing.basis: Emphasizes more housing types and faster, predictable permitting.

safety.basis: Supports officer recruitment and holding repeat offenders accountable, alongside stronger crisis-response systems.

experience.basis: First-time candidate ('First time public servant'), running against an incumbent.

healthcare.basis: Supports wider access, price transparency, and fewer surprise bills within the existing system; no universal-coverage proposal.

social.basis: Endorsed by Washington State Stonewall Democrats; no stated position on LGBTQ+ or reproductive policy.
